title: How close can pure functional programming get to C?
summary: This article explores how closely pure functional programming can approach the performance, control flow, and low-level characteristics of C. It examines the practical trade-offs between functional abstractions and C's efficiency and expressiveness, aiming to clarify how much of C-like programming is achievable without sacrificing functional purity.
problem_solved: It evaluates the technical and performance trade-offs involved in writing low-level systems-style code using pure functional programming rather than C.
why_valuable: It helps developers understand whether functional programming can provide C-level capabilities while retaining benefits such as referential transparency, safer abstractions, and easier reasoning.
